title: Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.01207v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When training large language models with reinforcement learning, terminal rewards provide little guidance about which steps matter. Common methods for assigning step credit overlook that work built on uncorrected mistakes is wasted while independent work remains valid. With only a final success/failure reward, every step in a failed episode has zero total future reward, even when it made progress. We propose Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping (DARS), which represents task progress as predicates linked by prerequisite relations and assigns step-level credit over the dependency graph. An annotator marks which predicates each step verifies, invalidates, or repairs. Verified predicates are discounted according to graph distance from the nearest broken prerequisite, while independent predicates are unaffected. translated_title: 面向智能体强化学习的依赖感知奖励塑形
translated_abstract: 当使用强化学习训练大语言模型时，终端奖励对于哪些步骤真正重要几乎没有提供指导。常见的步骤信用分配方法忽略了一个事实：建立在未纠正错误之上的工作是无效的，而独立的工作仍然有效。在仅有最终成功/失败奖励的情况下，失败回合中的每一步其总未来奖励都为零，即使该步骤已经取得了进展。我们提出依赖感知奖励塑形（DARS），该方法将任务进度表示为通过先决条件关系相互连接的谓词，并在依赖图上分配步骤级信用。标注者标记每个步骤验证、失效或修复了哪些谓词。已验证的谓词会根据其与最近的失效先决条件之间的图距离进行折扣，而独立的谓词不受影响。修复操作会根据仍存在的错误更新这些权重；被失效的谓词需要重新验证才能恢复信用。固定势能函数……
tldr: 本文提出依赖感知奖励塑形（DARS），通过将任务进度表示为由先决条件关系连接的谓词依赖图，并依据谓词与失效先决条件的图距离来分配步骤级信用，从而解决了强化学习训练大语言模型时终端奖励无法指示哪些步骤有效的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Dependency-Aware Reward Shaping (DARS), which represents task progress as predicates linked by prerequisite relations and assigns step-level credit over the dependency graph, addressing the problem that terminal rewards offer little guidance on which steps matter when training LLMs with reinforcement learning.
